answer:
**Positive-pair agreement alone admits a useless solution: make every embedding identical.** If the objective only pulls two views of the same example together, a constant vector gives zero distance for every pair. Low training loss then says nothing about whether different examples remain distinguishable. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.07733) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00020)

Contrastive methods introduce negatives, so the matched example must be preferred over alternatives. A constant representation cannot accomplish that discrimination.

**BYOL uses a different asymmetry.** An online network with a predictor matches a slowly updated target network, and gradients do not flow through the target branch. Its full training dynamics can learn useful features without explicit negative pairs. Stop-gradient by itself is not a general theorem preventing collapse; predictor, normalization, augmentation, and optimization choices matter.

Monitor per-dimension variance, covariance or effective rank, and downstream performance. A representation can look numerically nonconstant yet still preserve little useful information. Positive alignment and discrimination or feature diversity must be assessed together rather than declaring success because an alignment loss became small.

**Technical details and references.**

With only positive-pair distance minimization, a constant embedding makes every positive pair identical and can minimize the objective. Contrastive learning adds competing negatives so identical outputs cannot distinguish the matched item from other candidates. BYOL instead uses an online predictor, a slowly updated target network, and stop-gradient on that target; its complete training dynamics avoid collapse empirically without explicit negatives. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.07733) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00020)

Stop-gradient alone is not a general mathematical guarantee against collapse. Architecture, normalization, predictor dynamics, augmentations, and optimization matter. Track embedding variance, covariance/effective rank, and downstream linear-probe quality. A low alignment loss is insufficient evidence of useful representations: both a meaningful invariant representation and an all-constant representation can align positive pairs perfectly.
